title: CLR/53/2019 of BRAHMKALI Vs KARNWAL ASHRAM BHIMGAUDA HARIDWA

paras.text:
CLR No. 53 of 2019
Honíble Lok Pal Singh, J.
Mr. Narendra Bali, Advocate for the
revisionist.
 Mr. Sudhir Kumar, Advocate for the
respondent.
 Present civil revision has been filed
against the order dated 02.02.2019 passed by
Judge SCC/2nd Additional District Judge,
Haridwar in S.C.C. No. 19 of 2016 ìShri
Karnwal Ashram Bhimgauda Haridwar Vs. Smt.
Brahmkaliî, whereby the application (paper no.
37C) under Order 15 Rule 5 C.P.C filed by the
respondent/landlord has been allowed.
Brief facts of the case are that SCC No. 19
of 2016 ìShri Karnwal Ashram Bhimgauda
Haridwar Vs. Smt. Brahmkaliî was filed by the
respondent/landlord against the revisionist for
ejectment and recovery of rent of the property in
question. During the pendency of the suit, the
revisionist has filed an application under Order
7 Rule 11 read with Section 151 C.P.C. stating
therein that the tenant/revisionist is living on
contractual basis, therefore, the suit is not
maintainable. Against the said application,
respondent has filed his objections stating
therein that the said application is liable to be
rejected. Plaintiff/respondent moved an
application under Order 15 Rule 5 of CPC
before learned Judge, Small Causes Court for
striking off the defence of defendant (revisionist
herein) on the grounds, inter alia, that the
defendant has not been able to deposit the
entire rent amount, therefore, his defence was
liable to be struck off. The revisionist/defendant
filed her written statement denying the plaint
averments. At the time of filing the written
statement, revisionist also moved an application
with the prayer that the written statement has
been filed with delay, therefore, the delay may
be condoned and the written statement be
taken on record
The trial Judge vide order dated
02.02.2019 rejected the said application.

Before further discussion, it is apt to
reproduce Order 15 Rule 5 of C.P.C., which
reads as under:
ìStriking off the defence for failure to
deposit of admitted rent, etc.- (1) In any suit by
a lessor for the eviction of a lessee after the
determination of his lease and for the recovery
from him of rent or compensation for use and
occupation, the defendant shall, at or before the
first hearing of the suit, deposit the entire amount
admitted by him to be due together with interest
thereon at the rate of nine per cent per annum
and whether or not he admits any amount to be
due, he shall throughout the continuation of the
suit regularly deposit the monthly amount due
within a week from the date of its accrual, and in
the event of any default in making the deposit of
the entire amount admitted by him to be due or
the monthly amount due as aforesaid, the Court
may, subject to the provisions of Sub-rule (2)
strike off his defence.
Explanation 1:-- The expression 'first hearing'
means the date for filing written statement or for
hearing mentioned in the summons or where
more than one of such dates are mentioned in the
last of the dates mentioned.
Explanation 2:-- The expression 'entire amount
admitted by him to be due' means the entire gross
amount whether as rent or compensation for use
and occupation, calculated at the admitted rate of
rent for the admitted period of arrears, after
making no other deduction except the taxes, if
any, paid to a local authority in respect of the
building on lessor's account and the amount, if
any, deposited in any Court.
Explanation 3:--The expression 'monthly amount
due' means the amount due every month (sic) as
rent or compensation for use and occupation at
the admitted rate of rent, after making no other
deduction except the taxes, if any, paid to a local
authority, in respect of the building on lessor's
account.
(2) Before making an order for striking off defence,
the Court may consider any representation made
by the defendant in that behalf provided such
representation is made within ten days of the first
hearing or, of the expiry of the week referred to in
Sub-section (1) as the case may be.
(3) The amount deposited under this rule may at
any time be withdrawn by the plaintiff.
Provided that such withdrawal shall not have the
effect of prejudicing any claim by the plaintiff

disputing the correctness of the amount
deposited.
Provided further that if the amount deposited
includes any sums claimed by the depositor to be
deductible on any account, the Court may require
the plaintiff to furnish the security for such sum
before he is, allowed to withdraw the same.'
A perusal of the provisions of Order 15 of
Rule 5 C.P.C. would reveal that there are two
parts of Rule 5. The first part casts an
obligation upon the lessee-tenant to make the
payment of entire amount admitted by him to
be due together with interest thereon on the
first date of hearing failing which the Court has
power to strike off the defence of the
defendants. The second part envisages the
situation where the defendant even does not
admit any amount to be due but nonetheless an
obligation is cast upon him to pay throughout
continuation of the suit such monthly amount
which is due within a week from the date of its
accrual failing which the Court has got power to
strike off the defence.
Learned counsel for the respondent makes
a statement at bar that this Court may give at
least one opportunity to the revisionist and the
objections filed by the revisionist against the
application no.37C may be considered as
representation.
 Undisputedly, neither the revisionist has
deposited the rent due against her, on the date
of first hearing, nor she filed representation
before the Court below, but she filed the
objections against the application filed by the
respondent. Though, the revisionist has not
complied with the provisions contained in Order
15 Rule 5 C.P.C., having considered the
statement made by learned counsel for the
respondents, the trial court is directed that the
objections filed by the revisionist against the
application no.37C shall be considered as
representation made by her.
In view of the above, the impugned order
dated 02.02.2019 is hereby set aside. The
revisionist is permitted to comply with the
provisions contained under Order 15 Rule 5

C.P.C. within 15 days from today. The
revisionist shall deposit the entire due
outstanding alongwith 9% interest thereon
within three weeks positively and shall continue
to pay the rent by 7th of every month for use
and occupation. The trial court is further
directed to decide the matter as expeditiously as
possible, preferably within a period of six
weeks, in accordance with law.
In case, revisionist fails to comply with the
direction issued by this Court in permitting her
to deposit the outstanding dues within three
weeks from today the order passed by this
Court shall stand automatically vacated and
order passed by trial court stood revived.
